items.item_text: 01. Which statement below best describes the highest level of education you have completed? Options: Some High School | High school graduate, diploma or the equivalent (GED) | Some college (less than 60 units) | Associate degree or at least 60 semester units | Bachelor's degree | Master's degree | Professional degree | Doctorate degree

02. How many years of professional experience do you have providing oral interpretation and/or written translation services between English and Spanish? Options: No experience | Less than 1 year of experience | 1 year but less than 2 years of experience | 2 years but less than 3 years experience | 3 or more years of experience

03. Have you completed any of the following qualifications? Select all that apply. Options: Bachelor's degree in Spanish | College-level coursework equivalent to a bachelor's degree in Spanish | Specialized certificate program in interpretation and translation | None of the above

04. Which of the following types of written materials have you professionally translated between English and Spanish? Select all that apply. Options: Educational or instructional materials | Legal, medical, or technical documents | Business correspondence, reports, or administrative documents | Government forms, policies, or public notices | Marketing materials, presentations, or public communications | Other professional documents | No professional written translation experience

05. Which of the following interpretation methods have you used in a professional setting? Select all that apply. Options: Consecutive interpretation (interpreting after a speaker pauses) | Simultaneous interpretation (interpreting while a speaker is speaking) | Sight translation (orally translating written documents) | Remote interpretation by telephone or video conference | No professional oral interpretation experience

06. If you indicated having professional oral interpretation or written translation services experience in the previous question, please describe where and how you gained this experience, including: a) Names of employers b) Dates of employment c) Duties performed. If you do not have this experience, please indicate "N/A."

07. This position may require occasional evening assignments and travel between District schools, offices, and other assigned locations. Are you willing and able to meet these requirements? Options: Yes | No

Translates written District materials into the designated second language, including Individualized Education Plans (IEPs), Single Plans for Student Achievement (SPSAs), Local Control and Accountability Plans (LCAPs), bulletins, presentations, parent correspondence, and other instructional materials.

Interprets orally between English and Spanish for limited-English-proficient individuals at Board, IEP, parent/teacher, student, and other District meetings, conducted in person, by telephone, or through video conferencing, using consecutive and simultaneous interpretation as appropriate.
Performs sight translation, reading aloud in the designated second language from English-language documents during meetings and conferences as needed.
Reviews source materials for meaning and context, verifies intent with District personnel as needed, and produces accurate, clear, idiomatic translations suited to the audience and tone.
Develops and maintains bilingual glossaries and terminology references to ensure consistent, accurate translation of District and education-specific terms.

Formats, maintains, and files translated and interpreted materials in a variety of formats, including word processing documents, presentations, spreadsheets, and forms; prepares reports in the designated language.
Provides voice-over narration in the designated language for District audio and video recordings.
Performs related duties as assigned.
Grammar, vocabulary, syntax, spelling, punctuation, and idiomatic usage of both English and the Spanish, in oral and written forms.
Translation and interpretation practices and techniques, including consecutive, simultaneous, and sight translation.
Operation of standard office equipment and specialized language and translation software and tools.
Recordkeeping and reporting practices.
Techniques for communicating effectively, with tact, patience, and courtesy, with students, families, staff, and community members from diverse backgrounds.
District terminology, policies, and procedures.
Laws, regulations, and District policies governing the confidentiality of student and education records.
Translate written materials and interpret oral communication between English and Spanish.
Proofread, review, and edit translations for accuracy, clarity, and formatting.
Estimate translation time, prioritize assignments, and meet deadlines while managing multiple tasks.
Recreate and format documents in a variety of formats using standard office equipment and software applications.
Maintain records, files, and reports.
Work independently with minimal direction, and work effectively under pressure and frequent interruptions.
Maintain the confidentiality of sensitive and privileged information.
Model communications and interactions that respect and include all individuals and their languages, abilities, religions, and cultures.
Communicate orally and in writing with staff, students, parents, and members of the public.
